title: ValidationReport
description: What the deterministic validator says about a layout (5.5). This is what the UI shows, so every violation carries a measured value and a human sentence: never an opaque AI opinion. Produced identically by workers/layout/validator.py and packages/geometry/validator.ts; fixtures/validation/*.json pins the two together in CI.

fits.description: The headline. True when there is no hard violation. Soft violations are warnings and do not clear this flag.

violations.description: Global violations, i.e. ones that are not about a single item: circulation (H6), total price (H7), main walkway (S1).

items.description: Per-item findings, keyed by layout item id.

measured.description: Numbers the UI can show even when nothing is wrong: narrowest walkway, total price, free floor fraction.

code.description: The rule ids from the 5.5 tables. Closed list so violations can be counted and tested rather than grepped.

severity.description: Hard blocks an AI layout and shows red in manual editing. Soft is a warning the user may ignore.

message.description: The sentence shown to the user, with the measurement in it. For example: walkway narrows to 710 mm between the sofa and the bookshelf.

measured_mm.description: The value that triggered the rule, where the rule is about a distance.

limit_mm.description: The threshold it failed against, so the UI can say by how much.

related_ids.description: Other items, walls, openings or obstacles involved. An overlap is never about one item alone.
